name: Unix domain sockets instead of TCP loopback for same-host IPC (Extreme C ch. 20 calculator)
listed_description: Book says that for single-host deployments Unix domain sockets are preferred over network sockets; its calculator example implements both stream and datagram variants of each.
claim_text: UDS are preferred because they are faster, and they have less overhead in comparison to network sockets.
book_benchmark: No timings given; qualitative statement only. Companion code in ch20-socket-programming has UDS stream and datagram plus TCP and UDP servers and clients, but the book does not measure them.
found_in: book: Extreme C (2019), PDF section 'Socket programming review' in Chapter 20 (Socket Programming), chunk-05 line ~379
